main_text.p: Euangelij doctrinam non recte intelli-gentium, siue sint in Ecclesia, siue extra eam. Præsertim verò sapientiam huius mundi ab Euangelij doctrina seiungit: deinde sapietiam, quæ mundo stultitia est, declarat. Est autem humana sapietia parua quædam particula legis moralis, quod attinet ad externorum membro-rum gubernationem, seu quod alibi Philosophi vocant externam disciplinam: interea nihilominus in mente hærét dubitationes, in voluntate & corde fremitus & furores contra Deum dominatur. Quàm porrò egregios hæc fructus profe-rat, potest nobis exemplo quasi ob oculos ponere Pharisæus ille tumidus, qui commendans suam probitatem, virtute & sapientiam, particulatim recensebat, se de omnibus bonis decimas dare, ieiunare bis in septimana, &c. Huic similes passim Christus in Euangelio taxat. Quamobrem quantumuis pro sapientibus tales habentur & coluntur: tamen omnes naturali sua luce non intelligunt sapientiā Dei: de qua non aliter loquuntur & iudicāt, quàm eam sibi videri stultissimam concionem. Si igitur doctrina ecclesiæ
[Note: the words "tamer" and "sapientiā" and "ecclesiæ" are read with some doubt; the ends of several lines are faint.]

page.notes: The right margin shows faint text of the facing page (a header "DE..." and fragments of notes), which is show-through or the neighbouring page edge and is not transcribed. "tamer" at the end of a line is probably "tamen" with the n lost in the scan. The catchword "ecclesiæ" is doubtful. Line-end hyphens are kept as printed.
